original_question: Let w be a group word, and G a profinite group. Is it true that the cardinality of the set of w-values in G is either finite or at least continuum? An affirmative answer is known for several important words; see(E. Detomi, B. Klopsch, P. Shumyatsky, J. London Math. Soc. (2), 102(2020), 977–993).
target_in_paper: Open problem 21.122 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of arXiv:1401.0300 (The Kourovka Notebook, current arXiv version), page 178.
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the two parameters (a group word w and a profinite group G), asks exactly for the cardinality dichotomy for the set of w-values, and even reproduces the paper's accompanying note that an affirmative answer is known for several important words, with the same 2020 Detomi–Klopsch–Shumyatsky reference.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, w should be written as a group word in finitely many variables, say w = w(x1, ..., xn).
The set of w-values should be defined explicitly as {w(g1, ..., gn) : g1, ..., gn in G}.
The quantifiers should be made explicit: the question asks whether this holds for every group word w and every profinite group G.
The phrase "at least continuum" should be made explicit as cardinality at least 2^{aleph_0}.

It should be stated that no extra assumptions are imposed on w or G; in particular, the problem is not restricted to multilinear commutator words, Engel words, nilpotent profinite groups, or finitely generated profinite groups.

To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain about the image set of w itself, not about finiteness of the verbal subgroup w(G); nearby problem 21.105 introduces the notation Gw for word values and w(G) = <Gw>, but 21.122 asks only about the size of Gw.
refined_question: For every group word w = w(x1, ..., xn) and every profinite group G, must the set of word values Gw = {w(g1, ..., gn) : g1, ..., gn in G} be either finite or of cardinality at least 2^{aleph_0}?
justification: The draft is targeting open problem 21.122 exactly: the wording in the paper is essentially the same, including the literature note pointing to the 2020 paper of Detomi, Klopsch, and Shumyatsky. The only refinements needed are to make the set of w-values explicit, state the universal quantifiers, and spell out "continuum" as 2^{aleph_0}. Nearby problem 21.105 is the relevant local context because it defines the notation Gw for the set of word values and w(G) for the verbal subgroup, which clarifies that 21.122 is the narrower cardinality question about Gw itself, with no additional hypotheses on the word or the profinite group.
